hero.heading: Every module is open. The registry is yours to extend.
hero.description: Converged is not a box with sealed internals. Repositories, lambdas, surfaces and workflows all live in the source tree: read them, fork them, rewrite one for your own machines, contribute it back. The list below is assembled from that tree on every build, so a new module appears here exactly when it appears in the code.

stats.heading: What is in the registry today

labels.repository: repositories — persistent data domains and their APIs
labels.workflow: workflows — processes on the DAG runtime

items.title: The source tree is the only source of truth
items.description: This page is produced by walking the module tree. No list on it is hand-maintained, so the documentation cannot drift from the code: if it drifted, someone deleted a module.

items.title: A module is a directory
items.description: To add a module, create a folder that follows the naming convention and put a README beside it stating its purpose and ownership boundary. The build picks it up without a registry edit.

items.title: Boundaries are held by contracts, not by trust
items.description: Modules communicate through typed NRPC contracts over the bus. Each repository owns its storage volume, while lambdas receive no persistent mount.

items.title: Anyone can add a module
items.description: A machine adapter, a payment integration, an industry-specific workflow, one extra screen — all of it is added the same way the base modules are. What is useful to others goes into the shared registry; what is specific stays in the deployment.

items.title: Review, not a free-for-all
items.description: Open does not mean unchecked. A module must declare its area of responsibility, respect the architectural boundaries, and never ask for wider access than it needs.

items.title: Assembled for your shop
items.description: The same modules compose into different profiles: a 3D printing bureau, a CNC job shop, a lab, a network of sites. The solution decides the composition — not a build flag.

solutions.title: Modules ship in sets
solutions.description: A solution bundles repositories, lambdas, surfaces and workflows that together cover a whole area of work. The composition and dependencies below are read from solution files in the sources.
solutions.note: A dependency means the solution will not come up without it: enable AI and you get security with it.

registry.title: Every module, by domain
registry.description: The full list of what the repository holds. A domain is a folder in the source tree; a module's purpose is the first paragraph of its README.
registry.note: A module need not belong to any solution: it exists, and you can wire it in by hand or fold it into a solution of your own.
